extracted.intended_audience: Authors and researchers reporting healthcare quality improvement projects (clinicians, improvement scientists, journal editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing scholarly reports of healthcare quality improvement (QI) work, including planning, implementation, evaluation, and manuscript content to enable sharing and interpretation of QI interventions and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of theory
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 emphasises the reporting of the use of formal and informal theory in planning, implementing and evaluating improvement work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any formal or informal theoretical rationale that informed the design, implementation, or evaluation of the improvement effort (i.e., state the theory, assumptions, mechanisms or conceptual model used in planning, implementing and evaluating the work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 emphasises the reporting of the context in which the work is done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report contextual factors (setting, organizational, cultural, resource, and other environmental conditions) that could influence the intervention, its implementation, and the generalisability of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of the intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 emphasises the reporting of the study of the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe the methods used to study and evaluate the intervention(s), including study design, measures, analysis, and how the evaluation addressed effectiveness, implementation, and any unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report range and complexity of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 is intended for reporting the range of methods used to improve healthcare, recognising that they can be complex and multidimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail about the diverse and potentially complex methods used (qualitative, quantitative, mixed methods, iterative cycles, etc.), so readers can understand the approach, reproduce or adapt the work, and appropriately interpret findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SQUIRE as common reporting ground
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 provides common ground to share discoveries in the scholarly literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align reporting with SQUIRE 2.0 to improve clarity and comparability of QI reports, facilitating dissemination and critical appraisal of improvement studies.
